review.brief: Review tier 2 of RM57: charging.supercharger_sessions and charging.mirror_watermarks re-keyed on tesla_id. Read the branch diff against main, not the whole module. Validate: (1) every DB object matches the user-confirmed design in design.md - DDL, the UNIQUE (session_id) swap, tesla_id NOT NULL, the account_id drop, and the single index (tesla_id, charge_stop_date_time). Any mismatch is a blocker finding. (2) Module boundaries: no module reads another's DB; the gateway calls interfaces only; internal/app, internal/analytics and internal/gateway changes are leader-owned integration and must use charging's public ports. (3) Doc-pack conventions: km/C/PSI suffixes, internal/clock for time, bilingual i18n for any user-facing string. (4) Spec and tasks coverage: every requirement in specs/ is implemented; tasks.md matches what landed. (5) Tests assert the expectations design.md authored BEFORE implementation (its Test contract section), not whatever the code happens to do. Check T-1..T-13 specifically. (6) Three deletions need scrutiny, each claimed to be a design consequence rather than a weakened criterion: C7 and C11 in db_monthly_capacity_integration_test.go, and TestSuperchargerRowUpdate_NilTeslaIDSkipsRecalculationAndLogs in the gateway. All three needed a nil vehicle. Confirm a nil vehicle is now impossible, or raise it. (7) The per-vehicle mirror loop in internal/app/processor.go: confirm one car's cursor can never move past another car's unread rows, that a zero-row read never advances, and that the cursor never moves to now(). (8) VerifySession is re-keyed on tesla_id, not stripped. Confirm the gateway still proves ownership before the write. (9) Anti-gaming: no acceptance criterion weakened or deleted to finish, no self-approved status. Signals: the ASSISTANT ran go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, migration-guard, boundary-guard, vehicleref-guard, archive-guard and openspec validate --strict - all clean. The OWNER ran make test and reported it passed. You must NOT run the suite. Judge test quality by reading the tests.

findings.note: kkpa/context/use-case/charging/verify-session-battery.md (step 4, line 53, and the 'A nil TeslaID silently skips recalculation' bullet, lines 102-104) and kkpa/context/workflows/supercharger-stats-read.md (lines 81 and 83) still say recalculateAfterSessionVerify is skipped when Session.TeslaID is nil. T8.8 deleted that branch in internal/gateway/handlers/supercharger.go: recalculation now always runs, since tesla_id is NOT NULL. design.md's own 'Docs this change invalidates' table named both files for correction, but the nil-TeslaID claim in each survived.

New/changed comment lines cite design.md/RM/RD decision ids, e.g. internal/charging/charging.go's VerifySession doc ('...cannot tell not yours from does not exist (design.md D3)') and internal/charging/db/query.sql's LockSessionForVerification comment (new sentence: 'the whole tenant boundary on this write path now (design.md D3)'), plus several _test.go file headers ('Test -> Test Contract case mapping (design.md Test contract)'). The writing rule forbids this because design.md is archived and frozen. This mirrors a pervasive pre-existing codebase convention already used throughout this module (not invented by this change), flagged only because the rule is binding for lines this change added or changed.

No gateway test covers the new 'if !selOK' 404 branch added to SuperchargerRowUpdate (internal/gateway/handlers/supercharger.go, T8.7), and no test asserts VerifySession's teslaID argument equals resolveSelectedVehicle's resolved vehicle (the fixtures give every test account exactly one vehicle, so the passed value can't be distinguished from a wrong one). The real tenant boundary is proven at the DB layer (T-6, db_session_verifier_integration_test.go), so this is a coverage gap, not a security gap.

Re-checked: fixed. kkpa/context/use-case/charging/verify-session-battery.md and kkpa/context/workflows/supercharger-stats-read.md no longer claim a nil-TeslaID recalculation skip anywhere (grepped both files for 'nil' and 'TeslaID' - the remaining hits are unrelated, about battery-percentage nils). The unnamed extra fix is also confirmed: supercharger-stats-read.md line 67 now prints ListSessionsByVehicleBetween(ctx, teslaID, start, end) with no uid argument.

Re-checked: fixed. Repo-wide grep of every + line in *.go/*.sql since the tier-2 base (18cbe25) for design.md/RM##/RD# citations returns zero hits. Spot-checked several rewrites (charging.go's Session doc, query.sql's LockSessionForVerification, db_monthly_capacity_integration_test.go's C7/C11/T13 comments, db_session_verifier_integration_test.go, testdb_test.go): each kept the actual reason in the sentence and only dropped the archived pointer, not the substance. Confirmed out of scope, correctly untouched: query.sql lines with design.md D5/D1 that pre-date this change (present unchanged since 18cbe25) - the owner's scope decision (this change's own lines only) was applied correctly.

Re-checked: fixed, and this closes the gap I raised. TestSuperchargerRowUpdate_NoResolvableVehicleIs404 gives the account zero vehicles and asserts 404 plus zero VerifySession/Recalculate calls. TestSuperchargerRowUpdate_VerifyUsesResolvedVehicle gives the account two vehicles, makes the SECOND (index 1) the OWNER, and asserts VerifySession's teslaID argument is 22 (the resolved OWNER vehicle) - matches resolveSelectedVehicle's real selection logic (first OWNER wins over vehicles[0]) exactly, so an implementation passing the wrong vehicle would fail this test. Both tests are well-formed unit tests over fakes; no DB needed.
